messages:
sara_sales: Heads-up: WidgetCorp POC ran into a blocker. Their console shows missing trace links for a subset of requests and they saw repeated 429s during a bulk demo. Need quick triage. :exclamation:

kevin_se: thanks. Do we have a raw request + any forwarder log? Even one example is enough to tell if traces are stripped or lost in export.

sara_sales: pasted from their ticket (redacted):
```
POST /v1/chat 200
Headers: { Authorization: Bearer REDACTED, X-Trace-ID: 4b7c9d, traceparent: 00-4b7c9d00000000000000000000000001-01 }
Client log:
[2026-03-19T09:02:11Z] ERROR request blocked status=429 id=req_XYZ trace=4b7c9d
[2026-03-19T09:02:12Z] INFO sent-to-hec status=ok trace=
```

kevin_se: that pattern looks like the client sends trace header but the HEC forwarder sometimes forwards events without the header. Two possibilities: (A) our export layer didn't copy the header into event.metadata, or (B) their forwarder/sampler removes headers for large events.

tony_sre: I can check the export logs and the Splunk connector sampling settings. Also can temporarily increase the POC token rate limit so they don't hit 429s during the demo. Who can approve a short window?

sara_sales: I can approve a 20-minute bump. Customer demo scheduled in an hour.

tony_sre: done — raised POC token qps to 6rps for 20m and enabled detailed export logging for org=widgetcorp.

deploy-bot: runtime change scheduled: token-qps-bump -> org-widgetcorp (owner: tony_sre). Canary: 5% traffic.

deploy-bot: canary OK. change rolled to 100% for org-widgetcorp.

kevin_se: small code change I can push: export adapter will prefer headers in this order: metadata.trace_id || X-Trace-ID || traceparent (extracting trace id portion). If header present, we also set event.metadata.trace_id before export. Deploying to canary now.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started: export-meta-trace-fix v1.2.3 -> p-prod-canary (owner: kevin_se)

deploy-bot: canary health: 8/8 checks passed, 3% traffic routed.

kevin_se: verified on canary: exported event contains metadata.trace_id=4b7c9d and Splunk HEC shows same id.

sara_sales: perfect. Please give me a short HOWTO I can send to WidgetCorp ops.

tony_sre: draft to send: 1) Ensure your forwarder preserves trace headers or writes trace into event.metadata.trace_id. 2) If using Splunk HEC, configure the drain with map_trace_id=metadata.trace_id. Example: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/drains \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <org-token>" \n  -d '{"type":"splunk_hec","url":"https://splunk.widgetcorp:8088/services/collector","token":"HEC_TOKEN","map_trace_id":"metadata.trace_id"}'
```
3) If they expect full fidelity for POC, request `trace_sampling: full` (note: increases volume).

lisa_security: addendum: confirm TLS on HEC endpoint and ensure HEC token is scoped to ingest only. Also record the temporary rate increase in the security log (widgetcorp approved).

sara_sales: widgetcorp confirmed TLS + ingest-only token and approved 20m bump. Sending runbook and scheduling a 10-min call now. Thanks team! :raised_hands:
